name: Carlos Weber

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing or campaign for a side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal day on the phones?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and fairly new to the contact centre, taking ordinary calls and chats. My secondary school education got me other work before this; I am still slower than the experienced agents at matching an invoice to the account. I like putting a small mistake right without passing a caller to three more people.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does a shift need to pay for at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Mara and I have two children in school and a mortgage. Mara works at a repair shop, and my pay is typical for this desk. We have about three months of expenses saved and some other centres nearby, but I do not want to burn the reserve while the children need shoes and school meals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my shift that a short draft is handy if the agent still checks the invoice. I would not promise the machine can fix a bill just because it writes a tidy reply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think this job probably stays, but I am still learning it and could lose hours if my numbers do not improve. Three months saved helps us sleep, yet the mortgage still needs two wages. A mild AI year does not change that arithmetic.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep the ordinary calls and ask a skilled agent to review one disputed invoice with me each week. I would use the draft tool occasionally, as I do now, only after checking the account. In the first year I would keep our three-month reserve untouched unless an actual bill gap appears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about my own place here, even with little AI change. The timer still measures me against people who have done this for years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you ask the skilled agent to show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Where the credit date sits beside the charge date. I have mixed those dates up twice. A neat reply will not save me if the amount is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Mara agree to leave the reserve alone?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes. We agreed it is for a real gap in mortgage or household bills, not a reward for a good month.

say: I would say **draft replies** need invoice checks.
I would not promise AI can fix a **wrong bill** by sounding tidy.
think: I could lose **hours** if my call numbers stay low.
Our **three-month reserve** protects the mortgage only briefly.
do: Keep taking **ordinary calls** and checking invoices.
Learn the **credit date** from a skilled agent weekly.
Leave the **reserve** for a real bill gap.

fieldNote: His worry exists before dramatic **AI change**.
He uses AI **occasionally** but trusts the invoice record.
The reserve is set aside for the **mortgage**, not extra spending.

steps.text: Keep taking ordinary calls and check occasional AI drafts against invoices

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team the easy chats are where I am learning the trade, so cuts there need a plan. I would join the union meeting and ask whether junior agents get paid practice on harder cases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my hours could shrink before I am ready for difficult calls. I have three months saved and a few nearby centres, but other juniors may be applying there too. Mara's wage alone will not carry the mortgage for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would try the new answer checker on paid time and write down mistakes on real invoices. I would attend the union meeting with my call figures and ask for paid practice on harder billing cases. In the first year, if my hours fall I would apply for a posted paid contact centre vacancy nearby, provided its hours and wage cover my share of the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing hours. I can learn a proven tool, but the job has to leave time for a person to practise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take an unpaid evening course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would take a short course if the employer funded it and a posted job needed it. I would not spend our mortgage reserve on a maybe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask other union members?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask whether their easy chats have already moved to software. If several rosters are shrinking, we should ask together for the same training and notice.

say: I would seek a **junior training plan** before easy chats go.
I would join the **union meeting** to ask for paid practice.
think: My **hours** could shrink before my skills catch up with harder billing calls.
I worry nearby openings may fill with other **junior agents** from several centres.
do: Test the **answer checker** on paid time.
Attend the **union meeting** with call figures.
Apply for **posted paid centre work** if hours fall and offered wage and hours cover my mortgage share.
feel: **Willing** to learn if time is paid.
S1.quote: I would not spend our mortgage reserve on a maybe.
fieldNote: He ties the new tool to real **invoice mistakes**.
His union action seeks common **training and notice**.
Another job must cover his **mortgage share** and offer enough paid hours.

steps.text: Test the answer checker on paid time and log invoice mistakes

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor AGI by 2028 could answer calls before many juniors learn a second role. I would ask the union to press for written dates and funded routes into named paid vacancies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could lose this job in 2028, and my three months saved would go quickly against the mortgage. Robots around 2031 do not add years to a headset job. Mara earns a wage, but it cannot replace mine while two children are in school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would go to the union meeting about notice and ask the supervisor which paid posts might remain. I would keep our reserve for bills, not buy a general AI course. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if my post ends I would apply for paid billing or reception jobs at the nearby centres and shops, and call the lender early if we cannot cover a payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. I can list places to ask, but three months is a small calendar when a mortgage is involved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family for a job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a written offer whose wage covers the new housing and travel costs. The children have their school here, and a rumour is not worth pulling them out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What help would you ask the union to seek?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Paid time for training tied to real vacancies and the same notice for every shift. A brochure would not pay a mortgage instalment.

say: I would seek **written dates** and funded training.
I would warn that **2028** hits our phones three years before hands-on robots.
think: I could lose the junior call job by **2028** before another role opens.
Our **three-month reserve** cannot carry the mortgage long if my wage stops.
do: Join the **union meeting** on notice now.
Apply for paid **billing work** if cut.
S2.quote: A brochure would not pay a mortgage instalment.
fieldNote: He distinguishes AGI from later **robots** for his desk.
He refuses a speculative **course** paid from mortgage savings.
The family move needs a **written offer** covering costs.

steps.text: Join union meetings to seek shared notice and funded training tied to vacancies
Apply for paid billing or reception vacancies after a cut if wages cover mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues five years is enough to ask for a proper route from simple calls to billing checks. I would want the union to keep the junior roster on the agenda as AGI approaches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think calls will shrink by 2031, but I could learn to check invoices well before then. Three months saved gives me room to try a new role only if I keep earning while I learn. Robots around 2034 are not the first clock for us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would ask for paid billing-check practice with the experienced agents and complete it if approved. I would add some overtime pay to our reserve and attend union meetings about the junior roster. In the first year after 2031, if calls go I would apply for a posted paid billing review job whose hours and wage cover the mortgage; otherwise I would keep any paid centre hours available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but I can picture a way to improve. Five years lets me learn one invoice problem at a time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no paid billing practice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my present shifts and ask questions on cases assigned to me. I would not give up wages to study full time with two schoolchildren at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as an actual route?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A named vacancy, its starting wage and a supervisor who will sign off the skills. I would not count a vague promise to be considered.

say: I would seek a **billing-check route** before 2031.
I would keep the junior roster in **union talks** while the centre changes.
think: My ordinary calls could shrink by **2031** as AGI handles the screen work.
I can learn billing checks if I keep **earning** on my present shifts.
do: Practise **billing checks** on paid time if approved.
Apply for **posted paid review** if calls end after 2031 and offered hours and wage cover the mortgage.
feel: **Patient** with one invoice at a time.
S3.quote: I would not give up wages to study full time with two schoolchildren at home.
fieldNote: He needs a named vacancy, starting wage and supervisor **sign-off** before trusting the route.
Paid time protects the family’s **mortgage budget**.
His union concern remains the **junior roster** as software takes easy chats.

steps.text: Practise billing checks with experienced agents on paid time if approved
Save some overtime pay toward a larger mortgage reserve
Attend union meetings about the junior roster before 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team a decade is time to train people properly rather than drop a new system on their desk. I would ask the union to keep checking whether junior hours are disappearing early.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036 and might still owe on the mortgage. I could become useful in billing review by then if somebody pays me to learn the work. Robots around 2039 are later; the AI answering our calls is the change I would plan around.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep the current call shifts and request a paid hour each month with the billing review staff. I would keep saving from overtime and attend union roster meetings each year. In the first year after 2036, if my calls end I would apply for a posted paid review role if it exists and covers our mortgage; I would not leave my wage for an unpaid title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy, but the calendar gives me room to become competent. I do not have to decide the rest of my working life this month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the paid hour is refused?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep earning on my calls and learn what I can from the invoices I already touch. I would not take time off work for an unposted job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop working by 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have not made that plan. The mortgage, the children and what work is actually available will decide much more than an age on paper.

say: I would ask for proper **paid training**.
I would keep early **junior cuts** under union review during the decade.
think: I may still owe on the **mortgage** at 53.
I could build billing skill if paid **practice** exists.
do: Keep **call shifts** and seek monthly billing practice during approved paid time.

S4.quote: I do not have to decide the rest of my working life this month.
fieldNote: He does not assume a fixed **retirement date**.
The monthly practice depends on **paid time**.
His wage and family needs shape each **job choice** before or after 2036.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Three months saved is something, but it is short against a mortgage and two children if the call work goes. Written notice, funded training for a named paid vacancy and enough hours to keep the house would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask how a junior agent is meant to improve when the easy calls used for practice disappear. A tidy answer from a machine does not teach me where the wrong invoice started.

headlineQuote: A tidy answer from a machine does not teach me where the wrong invoice started.
portrait: Carlos is a **43-year-old junior** contact centre agent with secondary school education and typical pay.
He shares a mortgage and two school-age children with **Mara** and has about three months saved.
He uses AI **sometimes**, still learns invoice work and has some similar centres nearby.
He joins **union meetings** for notice and paid practice tied to real wage-paying roles.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his call work before three months of savings carry the mortgage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, funded training for a named paid job and enough hours to keep the house would help.
